title: Hydraulic Cylinder

introduction.definition: A hydraulic cylinder converts fluid pressure into straight-line force and motion. In a double-acting cylinder, oil fed to the cap end pushes the piston and extends the rod; oil fed to the rod end retracts it. Seals on the piston separate the two chambers; rod seals and a wiper in the gland keep oil in and dirt out.
key_points: Check rod buckling for long strokes
introduction.summary: A double-acting hydraulic cylinder turns oil pressure into straight-line force. Oil into port A pushes the piston and extends the rod; oil into port B retracts it. Force = pressure × area (the rod side has less area, so retract force is lower).

steps.text: Oil enters the cap-end port A.
Pressure on the full piston area pushes the piston and rod out.
Oil in the rod-end annulus returns through port B.
Reversing the ports retracts the rod.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Force ∝ pressure × area; speed ∝ flow / area — retract is faster than extend for the same flow because the annulus area is smaller.

pressure.title: Pressure while extending
pressure.description: Extending: port A feeds the cap end (red, system pressure) and port B returns oil from the rod end (blue, low). Push force F = p × A_bore. Retracting reverses the ports: the pull force is p × (A_bore − A_rod), smaller, but the rod moves faster for the same pump flow because the annulus volume is smaller.

annotations.text: Cap end: F_extend = p · π D²/4
Rod end (annulus): F_retract = p · π (D² − d²)/4

foundation: Mount on a level, rigid base with access for filters, gauges and fill; drip tray/bund under the reservoir.
alignment: Align motor and pump with the bell housing and coupling; mount cylinders so the rod is not side-loaded (use spherical bearings/clevises).
piping: Clean (pickled/flushed) pipework sized for velocity (typical guide: suction ≲ 1.2 m/s, pressure 3–6 m/s, return ≲ 3 m/s); hoses not twisted or rubbing; correct fittings for pressure.
Fit pressure gauges/test points, and relief protection on every pressure source.
commissioning: Fill through a filter with the specified oil; flush the system to the target cleanliness (ISO 4406 code).
Bleed air; start with relief valves backed off, then set pressures; check for leaks, temperatures and noise.

routine.task: Check rod for scoring and leaks at the gland.

overhaul.task: Re-seal; re-chrome or replace rod; hone barrel.

lubrication: Grease clevis pins and spherical bearings.

remedies: Replace seals; repair rod; improve wiper

causes: Side load, long stroke under compression

safety: Support loads mechanically before working on cylinders; release pressure; beware of trapped pressure (pressure intensification in the rod end if the port is blocked).

video_tutorials.title: Hydraulic Cylinder — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Hydraulic Cylinder.
A hydraulic cylinder converts fluid pressure into straight-line force and motion.
In a double-acting cylinder, oil fed to the cap end pushes the piston and extends the rod; oil fed to the rod end retracts it.
Seals on the piston separate the two chambers; rod seals and a wiper in the gland keep oil in and dirt out.
Typical applications include excavators, loaders and cranes; presses and injection moulding machines; gate, valve and damper actuation; steel and paper mills.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Barrel (honed tube), Cap End (clevis mount) & Rod-End Gland with Rod Seals / Wiper, Piston (with seals) & Chrome-Plated Rod.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Hydraulic Cylinder works.
Oil enters the cap-end port A.
Pressure on the full piston area pushes the piston and rod out.
Oil in the rod-end annulus returns through port B.
Reversing the ports retracts the rod.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Extending: port A feeds the cap end (red, system pressure) and port B returns oil from the rod end (blue, low).

video_tutorials.title: Hydraulic Cylinder — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hydraulic Cylinder.
Check rod for scoring and leaks at the gland.
Check mounting pins and bushes.
Re-seal; re-chrome or replace rod; hone barrel.
Watch for rod seal leak: oil on rod. Common cause: scored rod, worn seal, contamination.
Watch for internal leakage (piston seal): drift under load, slow. Common cause: worn piston seal, scored barrel.
Watch for rod buckling/bending: bent rod, seal damage. Common cause: side load, long stroke under compression.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
